title: The Windmill
subtitle: Torre vs Lasker, Moscow 1925 — thirteen moves of harvest.
goals: Sacrifice your queen for a windmill
Harvest an entire army with one rook

steps.say: Moscow 1925: 20-year-old Carlos Torre faces former World Champion Emanuel Lasker. Black's queen on b5 eyes White's queen on h5 — the g5 bishop is all that separates them along the fifth rank. Torre sees what that really means: if the bishop steps to f6, his queen hangs... and he WANTS that, because a rook landing on g7 can then give DISCOVERED CHECK over and over, capturing something new on every swing. A perpetual-motion capture machine. Chess calls it the WINDMILL, and this game is why.

steps.prompt: The queens attack each other — everyone in the hall expected a trade. Torre played the move of his life instead. Offer your QUEEN!
hints: What guards g7? Only the king. If your bishop lands on f6 first, Rxg7+ starts a discovered-check engine your queen's life happily pays for.
Bf6!! — if Black takes the queen, the windmill mills. If he doesn't, gxf6 wrecks his king anyway.

line.say: The queen hangs — Torre leaves her there. Lasker, a WORLD CHAMPION, took her, because declining loses too. Now the machine...
First check. The rook is untouchable — the f6 bishop guards it. The king shuffles, the rook swings, and each swing eats. Continue in the next challenge — the harvest deserves its own stage.

rejections.say: gxh6! — and with the g7 pawn gone to h6, the f6 anchor square loses its meaning: no windmill, queen traded for pawns. The queen is BAIT here, not a weapon: Bf6!!
...Qxh5 and now the queen is simply gone for nothing — only from f6 does the bishop guard the g7 windmill axle. One square, one immortal move: Bf6!!

steps.wrongSay: The move ignores both queens entirely. Which bishop square turns Rxg7+ into an engine?
steps.successSay: Bf6!! — a queen invested in a machine. Now run it.

steps.prompt: Lasker took the queen. Now run the full windmill — THIRTEEN moves: swing, check, capture, repeat, and come out ahead. The rook does everything.
hints: The cycle: Rxg7+ Kh8, then rook-takes-something-with-discovered-check, king returns, repeat. Order: g7, f7, back to g7, b7, back to g7... then finally capture the QUEEN on h5.
Rxg7+, Rxf7+, Rg7+, Rxb7+, Rg7+, Rg5+ (the exit!), and Rxh5 — count your loot at the end.

line.say: Blade one: the g7 pawn falls. The rook stands immune under the f6 bishop...
The swing OUT is a discovered check from the f6 bishop — so the rook eats f7 for free...
Swing back — check again. The king is a metronome and every tick costs Black material...
Blade three: the bishop on b7 falls to another discovered check...
Back once more. Torre could keep milling — but a great engineer knows when to stop the machine...
The exit swing — discovered check one final time, and the rook slides toward its true target...

HARVEST COMPLETE. The rook that started on g3 has eaten two pawns, a bishop and the QUEEN. Lasker fought on a few moves and resigned. Final ledger: Torre invested a queen and collected a queen, a bishop and three pawns. The windmill — once seen, never forgotten.

rejections.say: The exit before the harvest! You grabbed the queen line early — hxg5! and the rook dies: without the check-cycle Black gets to move. Every swing must CHECK: start with Rxg7+.

steps.wrongSay: Swing in with check, swing out with discovered check, eat on every swing. g7 first.
steps.successSay: A thirteen-move windmill against a former World Champion — you just re-enacted one of the greatest tactical sequences ever played.
